# `get_type_hierarchy`

Get the type hierarchy (super/sub-types, implemented interfaces) of an ABAP class or interface.

Defined in [`packages/adt-mcp/src/lib/tools/get-type-hierarchy.ts`](https://github.com/abapify/adt-cli/blob/main/packages/adt-mcp/src/lib/tools/get-type-hierarchy.ts).

## Input schema

| Parameter         | Type               | Required | Description                                                                           |
| ----------------- | ------------------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `baseUrl`         | `string`           | no       | SAP system base URL (e.g. https://host:8000)                                          |
| `client`          | `string`           | no       | SAP client number                                                                     |
| `username`        | `string`           | no       | Username for basic auth                                                               |
| `password`        | `string`           | no       | Password for basic auth                                                               |
| `systemId`        | `string`           | no       | Logical system id (resolved via multi-system config or ~/.adt sessions)               |
| `objectName`      | `string`           | yes      | Class or interface name (e.g. ZCL_MY_CLASS, ZIF_MY_INTF)                              |
| `objectType`      | `"CLAS" \| "INTF"` | no       | Object type: CLAS (class) or INTF (interface). Auto-detected if omitted.              |
| `includeSubTypes` | `boolean`          | no       | Whether to include sub-types (subclasses/implementors) in the result (default: false) |

## Output

The tool returns a single text content item whose body is a JSON-serialised object (`content[0].text`). On error, the response has `isError: true` and a human-readable message.

```json
{
  "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "<JSON.stringify(result, null, 2)>" }]
}
```

See the source for the exact shape of `result`.

## Example invocation

```json
{
  "name": "get_type_hierarchy",
  "arguments": {
    "baseUrl": "https://sap.example.com:44300",
    "username": "DEVELOPER",
    "password": "***",
    "client": "100",
    "objectName": "<objectName>"
  }
}
```
